info.name: ChatBot API — Admin panel
info.description:
# ChatBot API — admin panel

The requests the admin panel (dashboard) uses. Public sign-up, email activation pages, webhooks called by Meta / Paddle and developer tools are left out — they are in the full collection `ChatBotApi.postman_collection.json`. Plans, subscriptions, points and feature control are together under **Plans management (admin)**.

A multi-tenant RAG chatbot API (Django REST Framework). Every account (**tenant**) has its own knowledge (documents, API imports, website crawls), its own bot configuration, guided question tree and usage wallet. Everything you read or write is scoped to the signed-in account — another tenant's id is always a plain **404**.

Every request in this collection has a description (what it does, who can call it, fields, errors, frontend notes) and **saved example responses** captured from a real run of the API — open a request and pick an example from the *Examples* drop-down. Ids, keys and tokens in the examples come from a throwaway database.

## Base URL
`{{base_url}}` — production `https://chatbot-api.zaychain.com`, local `http://localhost:8000` (Docker: `http://localhost:8017`). Every path ends with a **trailing slash**.

## Authentication
| Method | Header | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| JWT (dashboard) | `Authorization: Bearer <access>` | Signed-in users in the dashboard. Get it from **Auth › Login**. |
| API key (integrations) | `X-API-Key: <key>` (or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`) | Server-to-server / embedded widget: chat, knowledge, documents, analytics. Paid feature — free-tier accounts get `api_key: null`. |

- Access token lives **3 days**, refresh token **30 days**. Refresh tokens are **single-use**: **Auth › Refresh token** returns a NEW refresh token — store it and drop the old one.
- On `401` call refresh once; if that fails, send the user to login.
- Accounts are created by an admin (**Users › Create user**). With an email they stay inactive until the user opens the activation link (**Users › Resend activation email** re-sends it).
- The collection sends `{{access_token}}` automatically; **Login** saves `access_token`, `refresh_token` and `api_key` for you.

## Roles
- **Tenant** (any signed-in user): own profile, own knowledge, chat, tree, config, analytics, billing view.
- **Admin** (staff): everything in folders marked *(admin)* — users, API keys, plans, subscriptions (assign / renew), points, feature overrides, WhatsApp accounts. Admin accounts can only be managed by their owner (another admin gets `403`).
Use `role` from `GET /users/me/` (`"admin"` / `"user"`) to show or hide admin screens.

## Conventions
- JSON everywhere except uploads (`multipart/form-data`, field `file`).
- Ids are **UUID strings**.
- Lists are paginated: `{ "count", "next", "previous", "results": [...] }`, 20 per page, `?page=N`. Most lists also take `?search=` and `?ordering=` (prefix `-` for descending).
- Dates are ISO-8601 UTC (`2026-10-08T09:30:00.123456Z`).

## Errors
- General: `{ "detail": "Human readable message" }`
- Validation (`400`): `{ "field": ["message", ...], "non_field_errors": [...] }`

| Code | Meaning in this API |
|---|---|
| 400 | Invalid input (see field errors) |
| 401 | Missing/expired token or bad API key → refresh or log in |
| 402 | Payment required: out of points, subscription expired, or a feature (API sync, crawl, API key) not on the plan |
| 403 | Not allowed: not an admin, account suspended, admin-on-admin action |
| 404 | Not found **or belongs to another tenant** |
| 413 | Document count / storage limit of the plan reached |
| 429 | Rate limited, or the plan's monthly question / token quota is used up (`detail` says which) |
| 409 | Conflict, e.g. renewing a subscription that is still running with points left |
| 503 | Upstream (LLM / embedding provider) temporarily down — nothing was charged; retry later |

## Plans, points and limits
- Every account has a **points wallet**. **1 point = $0.001 of real OpenAI cost.** Every operation that calls OpenAI is charged at its real cost:

| Operation | Typical cost |
|---|---|
| Chat answer (dashboard, API or WhatsApp), gpt-4o | ~12 points (gpt-4o-mini: < 1) |
| Indexing a document (upload / reindex) | ~1–2 points per 10 pages |
| Knowledge edit / resolving an unanswered question | a fraction of a point |
| Website crawl | ~10 points per 50 pages |
| API import (AI analysis + embeddings) | depends on the record count |
| Guided-tree translation (gpt-4o-mini) | ~1 point per language for a small tree |

- A chat answer **holds** up to 20 points before answering and is settled to its real cost after (released in full if it fails), so parallel requests can't overspend. The chat response carries `points_used` and `points_balance`.
- With **less than 1 point** left, or when the plan's period has **ended**, every one of those operations returns `402` until the admin renews. Reading (lists, the tree, analytics) keeps working.
- **Billing is manual**: an admin creates the plan (its `points` — rule of thumb `price × 250`), creates the user, assigns the plan (**Plans management › Subscriptions › Assign subscription**), and renews it (**Plans management › Subscriptions › Renew subscription**, only once it expired or ran out of points). Points **never roll over**; there are no point purchases.
- **No plan = free tier**: 300 points per calendar month, 1 document, 0.5 MB, no API sync / crawl / API key.
- Admins/staff are never charged.
- Render the billing page from **My plan & points › My subscription** (`points`, `renewal_reason`, `usage`) and **My points history**; gate buttons with **My features**.

## Rate limits (per account, per minute)
| Endpoint | Limit |
|---|---|
| `POST /chat/` | 60, and the plan's requests/minute (whichever is lower) |
| `POST /sync-api-content/`, `POST /crawl-website/` | 10 (shared) |
| `POST /documents/`, `/documents/upload-word/`, `/documents/{id}/reindex/` | 30 (shared) |
| `POST /users/change-email/`, `/users/request-password-code/` | 5 (shared) |
| `POST /auth/login/` | 10 per IP |
A `429` from a rate limit says `"Request was throttled. Expected available in N seconds."` — wait and retry.

## Long-running work (poll, don't block)
- **Uploads**: `processing_status` goes `pending → processing → completed | failed` — poll **Documents › Retrieve document**.
- **API sync**: `202` + `run_id` → poll **Sync API Content › Poll a sync run** until `done`.
- **Website crawl**: `202`; the new source appears under **Knowledge Content › Sources** when finished.
- **Tree translation**: poll **Guided Question Tree › List tree languages** while `translating` is `true`; `paused: true` means it waits for points.

## Languages
The dashboard is bilingual (Arabic/English). Chat answers follow `language` if sent, otherwise the question's language. The guided tree is authored in the canonical language (Arabic) and auto-translated into each language the account adds.

item.name: Auth

request.description:
**What it does** - Exchanges username + password for a JWT pair and returns the signed-in user's profile. Called by the login form.

**Access** - Public. Rate limit **10/min per IP** (`login` scope).

**Request** - JSON body:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | yes | matched exactly as stored (usernames are unique case-insensitively, but login uses the stored spelling) |
| `password` | string | yes | |

**Response** - `200`:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `access` | string (JWT) | valid **3 days**; claims include `user_id`, `username`, `is_staff` |
| `refresh` | string (JWT) | valid **30 days** |
| `user` | object | `id, username, email, email_verified, first_name, last_name, role ("admin"/"user"), api_key, is_active, date_joined` |

`user.api_key` is `null` for free-tier tenants (no active paid plan) and, in this response, also `null` for admin accounts; it is the key string for paid tenants.

**Errors**
- `400` `{"username": ["This field is required."]}` / same for `password`.
- `401` `{"detail": "No active account found with the given credentials"}` - wrong credentials **or** an account not yet activated / deactivated (same message either way).
- `429` throttled.

**Frontend notes** - Store `access` and `refresh`; send `Authorization: Bearer <access>`. Use `user.role` to decide whether to show admin screens (or decode `is_staff` from the token). When you get a 401 from login, hint "If you just signed up, check your email for the activation link". Don't rely on `user.api_key` from login for admins - call `GET /users/api-key/` instead.

request.description:
**What it does** - Trades a refresh token for a new access token. Call it when an API call returns 401 because the access token expired (or proactively before expiry).

**Access** - Public (the refresh token itself is the credential). No rate limit.

**Request** - JSON body:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `refresh` | string (JWT) | yes | the latest refresh token you hold |

**Response** - `200`:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `access` | string (JWT) | new access token (3 days) |
| `refresh` | string (JWT) | **new** refresh token (30 days) - refresh tokens rotate |

**Errors**
- `400` `{"refresh": ["This field is required."]}`.
- `401` `{"detail": "Token is invalid or expired", "code": "token_not_valid"}` (also for a token that was already used/blacklisted).

**Frontend notes** - Refresh tokens are **single-use**: rotation is on and the old refresh token is blacklisted. Always replace the stored refresh token with the one in the response, and serialize refresh calls (two parallel refreshes with the same token -> the second gets 401). On 401 here, clear storage and send the user to the login page. A deactivated user can still obtain an access token here, but it is rejected by every protected endpoint (401).

**What it does** - Checks whether a JWT (access or refresh) is well-formed, correctly signed and unexpired. Useful on app start to decide whether a stored token is still usable without hitting a real endpoint.

**Access** - Public. No rate limit.

**Request** - JSON body:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token` | string (JWT) | yes | access or refresh token |

**Response** - `200` with an empty object `{}` when valid.

**Errors**
- `400` `{"token": ["This field is required."]}`; `{"non_field_errors": ["Token is blacklisted"]}` for a refresh token that was already rotated.
- `401` `{"detail": "Token is invalid or expired", "code": "token_not_valid"}`.

**Frontend notes** - This only validates the token itself; it does not check that the user is still active. To load the user, prefer `GET /users/me/`, which validates the token **and** returns the profile in one call. On 401 try *Refresh token* once before forcing a re-login.

item.description: Sign in to the admin panel. **Login** saves `access_token` / `refresh_token` into the collection variables; **Refresh token** rotates them (refresh tokens are single-use). Accounts are created by an admin (**Users › Create user**), not by public sign-up.

item.name: Users
item.description: User accounts. Two audiences: **admins** (role `admin`) manage tenants - list, create, edit, delete, resend activation, set passwords, view/rotate API keys; **any signed-in user** uses the self-service routes on their own account - `me` (view/edit profile), the two-step verified email change (`change-email` -> `verify-email`), the two-step password change (`request-password-code` -> `change-password`) and `api-key` (view only, paid plans). Users can never rotate their own key; that is admin-only. Admin-on-admin actions (edit, delete, set password, view/rotate key) are refused with 403 - an admin account is managed only by its owner (or from the Django admin). Auth: JWT bearer, API key or session.

request.description:
**What it does** - Paginated list of every user account, for the admin "Users" table.

**Access** - JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`), API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`) or session. **Admin only** (`is_staff`). No rate limit.

**Request** - Query params, no body:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | string | no | case-insensitive match on username, email, first_name, last_name |
| `ordering` | string | no | `username` (default), `email`, `date_joined`; prefix `-` for descending |
| `page` | integer | no | 20 per page |

**Response** - `200` `{count, next, previous, results}`; each result:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID string | |
| `username` | string | |
| `email` | string | lower-cased; may be `""` |
| `email_verified` | boolean | |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string | |
| `role` | `"admin"` \| `"user"` | `admin` = staff account |
| `api_key` | string \| null | see note below |
| `is_active` | boolean | `false` = cannot log in |
| `date_joined` | ISO datetime | |

`api_key`: every tenant's key string (or `null` if none issued), your own key, but **`null` for every other admin** - a key authenticates as its owner, so the list must not print a colleague's.

**Errors**
- `401` missing/invalid/expired token or API key (e.g. `"API key is inactive."`, `"User account is inactive."`).
- `403` `"You do not have permission to perform this action."` - caller is not an admin.
- `404` `"Invalid page."` - page out of range.

**Frontend notes** - Show `role` and `is_active` / `email_verified` as badges; inactive + unverified users are waiting for activation -> offer "Resend activation". Hide Edit/Delete/Set password/API key actions on rows where `role` is `admin` and the id is not yours (those calls return 403), and hide Delete on your own row. Treat `api_key` as a secret: mask it with a reveal/copy button.

request.description:
**What it does** - Admin creates a tenant account, issues its API key, and can put it on a subscription plan in the same call. **Email verification is required**: if an email is given, the account is created **inactive** and an activation link is emailed; a user created without email stays active.

**Access** - JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`), API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`) or session. **Admin only** (`is_staff`). No rate limit.

**Request** - JSON body:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | yes | max 150; unique case-insensitively |
| `email` | string (email) | no | lower-cased; unique case-insensitively; triggers activation flow |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string | no | max 150 |
| `password` | string | yes | Django validators (min 8, not common, not numeric, not similar to user info) |
| `password_confirm` | string | yes | must match |
| `plan` | string | no | plan slug or UUID |
| `plan_duration_days` | integer | no | default 30 (only with `plan`) |

**Response** - `201`: the user object (`id, username, email, email_verified, first_name, last_name, role, api_key, is_active, date_joined`) where `api_key` is always the new key string, plus:
- `email_verification`: `"activation_sent"` | `"send_failed"` | `"not_sent"` (no email given).
- `subscription` (only when `plan` was sent): `{plan (plan name), status, current_period_end}`.

Assigning a plan resets the user's points to that plan's `points` (if the plan defines any).

**Errors**
- `400` field errors as in Register (`username`, `email` duplicates, `password` rules, `password_confirm`).
- `400` `{"plan": "Unknown plan (use a valid plan slug or id)."}` - checked before the user is created.
- `401` missing/invalid/expired token or API key (e.g. `"API key is inactive."`, `"User account is inactive."`).
- `403` `"You do not have permission to perform this action."` - caller is not an admin.

**Frontend notes** - After create, show the result row with an "Activation email sent" / "Email failed - resend" hint based on `email_verification`. `is_active` is `false` until the user clicks the link. Get the plan list from the subscriptions endpoints to fill a plan dropdown.

request.description:
**What it does** - One user's account details, for an admin "user detail" view or edit form.

**Access** - JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`), API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`) or session. **Admin only** (`is_staff`). No rate limit.

**Request** - Path param `id` (UUID). No body.

**Response** - `200`:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID string | |
| `username` | string | |
| `email` | string | lower-cased; may be `""` |
| `email_verified` | boolean | |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string | |
| `role` | `"admin"` \| `"user"` | `admin` = staff account |
| `api_key` | string \| null | see note below |
| `is_active` | boolean | `false` = cannot log in |
| `date_joined` | ISO datetime | |

`api_key` is the tenant's key string (or `null` if none), your own key when it's you, and `null` for any other admin. Retrieving another admin is allowed (read-only profile); only modifying them is refused.

**Errors**
- `401` missing/invalid/expired token or API key (e.g. `"API key is inactive."`, `"User account is inactive."`).
- `403` `"You do not have permission to perform this action."` - caller is not an admin.
- `404` `"No User matches the given query."` - unknown (or malformed) user id.

**Frontend notes** - Use `role` + id comparison with the current user to decide which actions to render (no edit/delete/password/key actions on other admins). Subscription, points and usage live in the subscriptions endpoints, not here.

404 Not Found — unknown or another tenant's id

request.description:
**What it does** - Admin edits a tenant's username, email, names, or active flag (deactivate/reactivate). PATCH for partial updates; PUT also exists and requires `username`.

**Access** - JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`), API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`) or session. **Admin only** (`is_staff`). No rate limit.

**Request** - Path param `id` (UUID). JSON body (all optional for PATCH):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | no | max 150; must be unique |
| `email` | string | no | set directly - **no verification**, `email_verified` is not changed |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string | no | max 150 |
| `is_active` | boolean | no | `false` blocks login and API-key use |
| `id`, `role`, `api_key`, `email_verified`, `date_joined` | - | - | read-only, ignored |

**Response** - `200` the updated user object (same fields as Retrieve).

**Errors**
- `400` `{"is_active": ["Admin/staff accounts cannot be deactivated."]}` - e.g. deactivating your own admin account.
- `400` `{"username": ["A user with that username already exists."]}` (exact-case duplicate). A duplicate email, or a username differing only in case, is not caught by validation and fails server-side - check uniqueness in the UI first.
- `401` missing/invalid/expired token or API key (e.g. `"API key is inactive."`, `"User account is inactive."`).
- `403` `"You do not have permission to perform this action."` - caller is not an admin.
- `403` `"Admin accounts can only be managed by their owner."` - target is another admin/staff account. Admin is one flat role, so without this guard any admin could take over any other; acting on your OWN account is always allowed.
- `404` `"No User matches the given query."` - unknown (or malformed) user id.

**Frontend notes** - Hide the edit action for other admins and the "Deactivate" toggle for any admin row (including yourself). Deactivating a tenant immediately makes their tokens and API key fail with 401. Self-service profile edits by a normal user go through `PATCH /users/me/` instead.

request.description:
**What it does** - Permanently deletes a tenant and everything they own - documents, knowledge, API key and subscription all cascade, with no undo.

**Access** - JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`), API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`) or session. **Admin only** (`is_staff`). No rate limit.

**Request** - Path param `id` (UUID). No body.

**Response** - `204` no content for an ordinary tenant.

**Errors**
- `400` `{"detail": "You cannot delete your own account."}`
- `403` `{"detail": "Admin accounts can only be managed by their owner."}` - target is any other admin/staff account (the code returns this 403, not a 400).
- `401` missing/invalid/expired token or API key (e.g. `"API key is inactive."`, `"User account is inactive."`).
- `403` `"You do not have permission to perform this action."` - caller is not an admin.
- `404` `"No User matches the given query."` - unknown (or malformed) user id.

Both refusals exist because neither can be repaired through the API: the admin role cannot be granted back via the API, so the last admin could otherwise be removed with no way in. An admin account that genuinely must go is removed from the Django admin.

**Frontend notes** - In the UI, hide the Delete button on the current user's row and on any row whose `role` is `"admin"` rather than letting the call fail. Always show a confirmation dialog stating that all of the user's documents and knowledge will be deleted. Remove the row locally (or refetch) on 204.

request.description:
**What it does** - Returns the signed-in user's own profile. Call it on app load (to validate the stored token and get role/name) and on the profile page.

**Access** - JWT, API key or session. Any signed-in user, acting on their own account. No rate limit.

**Request** - No body.

**Response** - `200`:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID string | |
| `username` | string | |
| `email` | string | lower-cased; may be `""` |
| `email_verified` | boolean | |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | string | |
| `role` | `"admin"` \| `"user"` | `admin` = staff account |
| `api_key` | string \| null | see note below |
| `is_active` | boolean | `false` = cannot log in |
| `date_joined` | ISO datetime | |

`api_key`: the key string for tenants on an active paid plan; `null` for free-tier tenants. For admin accounts this endpoint also returns `null` - use `GET /users/api-key/` to show an admin their key.

**Errors**
- `401` missing/invalid/expired token or API key (e.g. `"API key is inactive."`, `"User account is inactive."`).

**Frontend notes** - Use `role === "admin"` to show the admin area. Use `email_verified` to nudge users to verify a changed email. Don't use `api_key` from here to decide whether to show the API-key page - call `GET /users/api-key/` and handle 402 (upgrade prompt).

**What it does** - Lets the signed-in user edit their own username, first name and last name. Email is **not** editable here (use change-email -> verify-email); the API key is never editable.

**Access** - JWT, API key or session. Any signed-in user, acting on their own account. No rate limit.

**Request** - JSON body, all optional (partial update):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `username` | string | no | trimmed; cannot be blank; unique case-insensitively (your own current name is fine) |
| `first_name` | string | no | max 150 |
| `last_name` | string | no | max 150 |

Any other field (`email`, `is_active`, `api_key`, ...) is ignored.

**Response** - `200` the full updated user object (same fields as *Me*).

**Errors**
- `400` `{"username": ["Username cannot be blank."]}` / `{"username": ["That username is already taken."]}` / max-length errors.
- `401` missing/invalid/expired token or API key (e.g. `"API key is inactive."`, `"User account is inactive."`).

**Frontend notes** - Replace your cached user with the response. Changing `username` does not invalidate the current JWT, but the `username` claim inside the existing token stays stale until the next login - read the name from the user object, not the token. The user must log in with the new username next time.

**What it does** - Step 1 of the verified email change: emails a 6-digit code to the **new** address. The account email is NOT changed until the code is confirmed with *Verify email (confirm code)*. Requesting again invalidates the previous code.

**Access** - JWT, API key or session. Any signed-in user, acting on their own account. Rate limit **5/min per user**, shared with *Request password change code* (`email_code` scope).

item.description: Admin-only control plane for API keys across all tenants. An API key authenticates as its owner (`X-API-Key` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`), so these endpoints are effectively account-access controls. Every user gets one key (one per user) when created, so the usual flow is **List** -> pick a row -> **Revoke** / **Activate** / **Regenerate**; **Create** is only for a user whose key was deleted. Other admins' keys are hidden from the list and return 404 on every action (rotating/revoking a colleague's key would be an account takeover); your own key is yours to manage.

item.name: Plans management (admin)
item.description:
Everything an admin needs to sell and run plans. Billing is manual — the usual flow:

1. **Plans › Create plan** (name, price, points, limits).
2. **Users › Create user (admin)**.
3. **Subscriptions › Assign subscription** — the user gets the plan's points for `duration_days`.
4. Watch **Subscriptions › List subscriptions**: `points_balance`, `can_renew`, `renewal_reason`.
5. **Subscriptions › Renew subscription** once it expired or ran out of points.

Points never roll over and can't be bought. Admin/staff accounts are never charged. All requests here need an admin token (a tenant gets `403`).

item.name: Plans
item.description: Create and edit the plans you sell. A plan is a number of **points** per period (rule of thumb: `points = price_usd × 250`) plus limits (documents, storage, requests/min, LLM model, API sync). Changing a plan's limits applies to its subscribers immediately; a new `points` value applies from each subscriber's next assignment or renewal.

item.description:
The bot's main endpoint plus thumbs up/down feedback. Every request is scoped to the authenticated tenant (JWT or API key): answers come only from that tenant's knowledge and use its Chatbot Config.

Typical UI flow: keep the conversation as an array of `{role, content}` messages in client state (the server stores no chat history), send the new `question` together with the last few messages as `history`, render `answer` as Markdown, then optionally send `POST /chat/feedback/` when the user rates an answer.

request.description:
**What it does**
Answers a customer question with the RAG pipeline: it searches the caller's own knowledge (documents, API syncs, crawled pages, resolved Q&A) and has the LLM reply in the customer's language and dialect, following the tenant's Chatbot Config. This is the call behind the chat "Send" button. There is no streaming; the full answer comes back in one response.

**Access**
- Auth: JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) **or** tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` / `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any signed-in user.
- Rate limits: DRF throttle `chat` = **60/min per user**, plus the tenant's own per-minute cap `max_requests_per_min` (default 60; set per plan or per tenant).
- Quotas checked before answering, in this order: account suspended → subscription lapsed → per-minute cap → plan's monthly question quota → monthly token budget → points (at least 1 point left).
- **Points:** up to `CHAT_POINTS_RESERVE` (default **20**) points are held atomically *before* the answer is generated (parallel requests can't overspend), then settled to the real cost of the answer (its LLM call plus the question's embedding — ~12 points on gpt-4o) or released in full if the answer fails. With less than 20 points left the hold shrinks to what is left; below 1 point the chat returns `402`. Staff/superusers never spend points and skip the lapsed-subscription check.

**Request**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question` | string | yes | Max 2000 chars; cannot be blank. Any language. |
| `history` | array of `{role, content}` | no | Earlier messages, oldest first. `role` is `user`, `assistant` or `system`; `content` is a non-blank string. At most `CHAT_MAX_HISTORY_TURNS` × 2 messages (default 10 turns = **20 messages**). Default `[]`. |
| `language` | string | no | Max 8 chars, e.g. `ar`, `en`. Blank/omitted → detected from the question (any Arabic script → `ar`, otherwise langdetect, fallback `en`). |

**Response** — `200`
| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `answer` | string | Text to show. May contain Markdown (links are written as plain URLs). |
| `source` | string | Always `"rag"`. |
| `source_id` | string | Currently always `""`. |
| `sources` | array | Chunks given to the LLM: `{filename, document_id, chunk_id, position, score}` (ids are UUID strings, `score` is cosine similarity). Empty when nothing was retrieved. |
| `confident` | boolean | `true` when the model answered from the data or asked a clarifying question ("which one do you mean?"). `false` = knowledge gap, off-topic/greeting, or no data. |
| `response_time_ms` | integer | Server time for the answer. |
| `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens` | integer | LLM tokens used (0 when no LLM call was made). |
| `cost_usd` | number | Estimated LLM cost (0 for models without pricing). |

**Errors**
- `400` — field errors, e.g. `{"question": ["This field may not be blank."]}`, `{"history": ["History too long: keep the last 10 exchanges (at most 20 messages)."]}`, invalid `role`.
- `401` — no/invalid credentials: `Authentication credentials were not provided.`, `Given token not valid for any token type`, `Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`, `User account is inactive.`
- `403` — `This account is suspended. Contact the administrator.`
- `402` — `Your subscription has expired. Please renew to continue.` (had a subscription that is now expired/canceled).
- `402` — `You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan.` (from the pre-check or from the atomic hold).
- `429` — per-minute cap: `Rate limit exceeded (60 requests/min). Please slow down.` (number = the tenant's limit).
- `429` — question quota: `You've used all N questions in your plan for this period. Upgrade your plan or wait for the next cycle. (Only when the plan sets the optional `monthly_questions` cap.)`
- `429` — token budget: `Usage budget exhausted for this period. It resets next cycle.`
- `429` — DRF throttle: `Request was throttled. Expected available in N seconds.` (with a `Retry-After` header).
- `503` — `The assistant is temporarily unavailable. Please try again.` (LLM or vector search down). Nothing is charged.

**Frontend notes**
- The server keeps no history. Keep the messages yourself and send the last few as `history` (the dashboard sends the last 3; never more than 20 messages, or you get `400`).
- Follow-ups such as "and before him?" work because the server adds the last two history messages to the search query before retrieval. This is plain text joining, not an LLM rewrite.
- Show a typing indicator (replies usually take a few seconds). Render `answer` with a Markdown renderer.
- When `confident` is `false` you may show a subtle "not sure" hint. Questions the model marks as an in-domain *gap* are logged automatically in **Unanswered Questions**.
- `402` → "out of points / plan expired — contact the administrator". `429` → "slow down" or "quota reached" message (use `detail`). `503` → offer retry; the user was not charged.
- Points are still spent when the reply is a fallback (for example the configured `no_answer_message` when the knowledge base is empty).
- After each answer, update your points counter from `points_balance` (or refresh `GET /my-subscription/`).

**Points in the response** — `points_used` (number): what this answer took from the wallet; `points_balance` (number | null): the wallet after it (`null` for staff, who are never charged).

item.description:
A multilingual tree of tappable questions with canned answers (a guided chatbot menu), scoped to the tenant. One **canonical** language (`GUIDED_TREE_CANONICAL_LANGUAGE`, default `ar`) is written by hand. Every other active language is a generated mirror, matched to it by position (same `order` under the same parent) and translated by an LLM in the background.

Typical UI flow: load `GET /tree-languages/` for a language picker, then `GET /guided-tree/?language=<code>` to render the tree (tap a node → show its `answer` and `children`). Admin editor: `GET /guided-tree/flat/` + create/edit/delete nodes (edits always land on the canonical tree), add languages, and **poll `GET /tree-languages/` while `translating` is true** to show progress (`translated_nodes / total_nodes`).

Reading is always allowed. Creating nodes, retranslating and adding languages return `402` when the tenant's `guided_tree` feature is turned off (it is on by default).

Cached per tenant and language for `GUIDED_TREE_CACHE_TTL` seconds (default 300). Writes clear the cache.

| `language` (query) | string | no | Language code, e.g. `ar`, `en`. Default: the canonical language. Not validated; an unknown code returns an empty tree. |

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `language` | string | The language returned. |

request.description:
**What it does**
Forces a full re-translation from the canonical tree, for one language or for all of your active non-canonical languages. It runs in the background and **in place**: the language keeps serving its current tree until each node is replaced, so it is never empty. Nodes that no longer exist in the canonical tree are removed.

**Access**
JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) **or** tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any signed-in user; data is scoped to the caller (tenant). Requires the `guided_tree` feature; otherwise `402`. The translation calls are charged to the tenant's points; `402` `You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan.` when it has less than 1 point or its plan lapsed.

**Request**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `language` | string | no | One language code. Omit (or send empty) for all of your active target languages (yours plus global ones, excluding the canonical language). The canonical code is ignored. The code is **not** checked against your language list. |

**Response** — `202 Accepted`
| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | Always `"retranslating"`. |
| `languages` | string[] | Languages queued. `[]` means nothing to do (e.g. you sent the canonical code). |

**Errors**
- `401` — no/invalid credentials: `Authentication credentials were not provided.`, `Given token not valid for any token type`, `Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`, `User account is inactive.`
- `402` — `The guided question tree isn't enabled for your account.`

**Frontend notes**
- After the `202`, poll `GET /tree-languages/` every few seconds while `translating` is true, then reload the tree.
- Only one sync runs per tenant at a time. A request made during a running sync is queued and runs after it.
- Only send codes from your language list. Any other code still creates a translated tree that no language entry points to.

**Points** — this calls OpenAI (translating the tree with gpt-4o-mini; ~1 point per language for a small tree. If the points run out, the remaining nodes stay untranslated (the language shows `paused: true`) and resume after the admin renews), charged to the tenant at its real cost. Returns `402` `{"detail": "You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan."}` when the tenant has less than 1 point, or `402` `{"detail": "Your subscription has expired. Please renew to continue."}` when its plan lapsed (staff are never blocked).

JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) **or** tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any signed-in user; data is scoped to the caller (tenant). Requires the `guided_tree` feature; otherwise `402`. `global: true` is admin-only (staff/superuser).

**Request**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | string | yes | Max 10 chars; trimmed and lowercased (e.g. `en`). Can't be the canonical code. |
| `name` | string | yes | Display name, max 64. |
| `is_active` | boolean | no | Default `true`. |
| `global` | boolean/string | no | `true`/`1`/`yes` → add for every tenant (admins only). |

**Response** — `201`: `id` (UUID), `code`, `name`, `is_active`. If the code already exists in the same scope, its `name` and `is_active` are updated (still `201`).

**Errors**
- `400` — `That is the canonical language; it already exists.` `That language is already available to every account.` (the code exists globally). Field errors (`code`/`name` missing or too long).
- `401` — no/invalid credentials: `Authentication credentials were not provided.`, `Given token not valid for any token type`, `Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`, `User account is inactive.`
- `402` — `The guided question tree isn't enabled for your account.`
- `403` — `Only admins can add a global language.`

**Frontend notes**
- After the `201`, poll `GET /tree-languages/` until `translating` is false and show `translated_nodes / total_nodes`.
- Before translation finishes, `GET /guided-tree/?language=<code>` may be empty or partial.
- The new language is translated right away even if you send `is_active: false`. Later edits only sync to active languages.
- A global language added by an admin is translated only for the admin's own tree right away. Other tenants get it at their next tree sync.

**Points** — this calls OpenAI (translating the tree with gpt-4o-mini; ~1 point per language for a small tree. If the points run out, the remaining nodes stay untranslated (the language shows `paused: true`) and resume after the admin renews), charged to the tenant at its real cost. Returns `402` `{"detail": "You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan."}` when the tenant has less than 1 point, or `402` `{"detail": "Your subscription has expired. Please renew to continue."}` when its plan lapsed (staff are never blocked).

**What it does**
Removes a language from your tree and deletes every node translated into it. If the code is a **global** language (and not one of yours), only admins can remove it, and it is removed for every tenant that hasn't also added it themselves.

**Access**
JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) **or** tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any signed-in user; data is scoped to the caller (tenant). Not feature-gated. Removing a global language requires staff/superuser.

**Request**
| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` (path) | string | yes | The language **code** (e.g. `en`), not the row id. |

No body.

**Response** — `204 No Content`.

**Errors**
- `400` — `The canonical language cannot be removed.`
- `401` — no/invalid credentials: `Authentication credentials were not provided.`, `Given token not valid for any token type`, `Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`, `User account is inactive.`

Returns the caller's chatbot configuration. If none exists yet, it is created with defaults. Use it to fill the bot settings form.

**Access**

| `tone` | string | `friendly` (default) / `formal` / `concise`. |

- Show `null` retrieval values as "default" in the UI.

request.description:
**What it does** — Uploads a knowledge file; it is parsed, chunked and embedded on ingestion. Use for `.txt`, `.md` or `.docx` uploads.

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. Rate limit: `upload` scope, 30/min per account, shared by upload, upload-word and reindex. Document/storage quota: per-tenant override > active plan > defaults (100 documents / 200 MB; free tier 1 document / 0.5 MB). Max 20 MB per file. The quota check runs before the file is saved.

**Request** — `multipart/form-data` (do not set `Content-Type` yourself):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | file | Yes (in practice) | Extension must be `.docx`, `.txt` or `.md`; max 20 MB |
| `is_active` | bool | No | Default `true` |

**Response** — `201` with only the write fields: `{"file": "<media URL>", "is_active": true}`. No `id` is returned, and the `file` URL is not publicly served (use `download_url` from the document instead).

How fast it is processed depends on the server's ingestion mode: in-request (document is already `completed`/`failed` when the response arrives) or background (`pending` → `processing` → `completed`/`failed`).

**Errors**
- `400` field errors, e.g. `{"file": ["Unsupported file type '.pdf'. Allowed: .docx, .md, .txt."]}` or `{"file": ["File is too large (25.0 MB). Maximum allowed size is 20 MB."]}`.
- `413` quota: `Document limit reached (N). Delete some documents or request a higher limit.` or `Storage limit reached (X MB). Currently using Y MB.`
- `403` `This account is suspended. Contact the administrator.`
- `429` throttled: `{"detail": "Request was throttled. Expected available in N seconds."}`.
- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

**Frontend notes** — An ingestion failure (empty file, embedding outage) does NOT fail the upload: you still get `201` and the document ends up `failed` with `error_message`. Because the body has no id, re-fetch `GET /documents/?ordering=-created_at` and pick the new row, then poll it. For `.docx`, `upload-word` returns the full document and is more convenient. Always send `file`; omitting it is not handled cleanly by the server.

**Points** — this calls OpenAI (embedding the document's text; a 10-page document is ~1–2 points), charged to the tenant at its real cost. Returns `402` `{"detail": "You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan."}` when the tenant has less than 1 point, or `402` `{"detail": "Your subscription has expired. Please renew to continue."}` when its plan lapsed (staff are never blocked).

| Field | Type | Notes |

| `filename` | string | Original file name, or the sync/crawl `document_name` |
| `file_size` / `file_size_mb` | int / float | Bytes / MB (0 for API/website) |
| `chunk_count` | int | Searchable pieces currently indexed |

| `error_message` | string | Why it failed ("" otherwise) |

| `source_type` | enum | `file` \| `api` \| `website` |

| `uploaded_by`, `uploaded_by_username` | int, string | Owner |

**What it does** — Partially updates a document. In practice it toggles `is_active` (whether the bot may answer from it). `PUT /documents/{id}/` also exists with the same fields; neither field is required there either.

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. Only your own documents. No rate limit, and no quota check.

**Request** — JSON or `multipart/form-data`.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (path) | UUID | Yes | |
| `is_active` | bool | No | `false` keeps the document and its knowledge but excludes it from chat retrieval |
| `file` | file | No | Replaces the stored file (`.docx`/`.txt`/`.md`, max 20 MB) |

**Response** — `200` with only the write fields: `{"file": "<media URL or null>", "is_active": false}`. Re-fetch `GET /documents/{id}/` for the full object.

- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. Only your own documents. No rate limit.

|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (path) | UUID | Yes | |

**Response** — `204 No Content`.

**Errors**

- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

**Frontend notes** — Confirm first: there is no undo, and the bot stops answering from it immediately. Deleting frees document-count and storage quota, so it is the fix for a `413` on upload. request.description:
**What it does** — Forces re-chunking and re-embedding of an existing document from its stored file. The old pieces are replaced, and hand-made corrections are lost.

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. Only your own documents. Rate limit: `upload` scope, 30/min per account, shared by upload, upload-word and reindex. No quota check.

|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (path) | UUID | Yes | |

- `500` `{"detail": "Re-indexing failed. Please try again later."}`: parsing or embedding failed (in-request mode). The document is marked `failed` with `error_message`; its old pieces are kept because they are only replaced after embedding succeeds.
- `429` throttled: `{"detail": "Request was throttled. Expected available in N seconds."}`.
- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

API and website sources have no stored file, so a reindex fails (`500` in-request, or `failed` later) and flips the document to `failed`. For those, re-run the sync or crawl instead. Warn the user that edits made through `/knowledge/` are overwritten. Poll `GET /documents/{id}/` when the response is not final.

**Points** — this calls OpenAI (re-embedding the whole document), charged to the tenant at its real cost. Returns `402` `{"detail": "You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan."}` when the tenant has less than 1 point, or `402` `{"detail": "Your subscription has expired. Please renew to continue."}` when its plan lapsed (staff are never blocked).

request.description:
**What it does** — Downloads the original uploaded file. This is the only way to read it, because the media directory is not publicly served. Every document's `download_url` points here.

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. Owner only (another tenant's id is a 404). No rate limit.

**Request** — No body.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (path) | UUID | Yes | Document id |

**Response** — `200` with the raw file bytes (not JSON). `Content-Type` is guessed from the filename (fallback `application/octet-stream`). `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename*=UTF-8''<original filename>`, so files are never rendered inline.

**Errors**
- `404` unknown or foreign id.
- `404` `This document has no stored file.`: API-synced and crawled documents (their `download_url` is `null`).
- `404` `The stored file is missing.`: the file is gone from storage.
- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

**Frontend notes** — A plain `<a href>` cannot send the JWT/API-key header. Use `fetch(download_url, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`}})`, read `res.blob()`, then trigger a save via `URL.createObjectURL`. Take the file name from `Content-Disposition` (decode the `filename*` value) or from the document's `filename`. Hide the button when `download_url` is `null`.

request.description:
**What it does** — Uploads a Word `.docx` file; it is parsed, chunked and embedded immediately (or in the background, depending on server ingestion mode). Unlike `POST /documents/`, it returns the full document.

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. Rate limit: `upload` scope, 30/min per account, shared by upload, upload-word and reindex. Document/storage quota: per-tenant override > active plan > defaults (100 documents / 200 MB; free tier 1 document / 0.5 MB). Max 20 MB per file.

**Request** — `multipart/form-data`:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | file | Yes | `.docx` only (not `.doc`); max 20 MB |

**Response** — `201` with the document (id, download_url, filename, file_size, file_size_mb, chunk_count, processing_status, error_message, is_active, source_type, api_url, items_key, uploaded_by, uploaded_by_username, created_at, updated_at) plus `chunks_created` (int). In-request mode: status is `completed` and `chunks_created` > 0. Background mode: status `pending`/`processing` and `chunks_created` is `0`.

**Errors**
- `400` `A 'file' field is required.`
- `400` `Unsupported file type '.pdf'. Upload a Word .docx file.`, `File is too large (X MB). Maximum allowed size is 20 MB.`, or `Document is empty.`
- `413` quota: `Document limit reached (N). Delete some documents or request a higher limit.` or `Storage limit reached (X MB). Currently using Y MB.`
- `403` `This account is suspended. Contact the administrator.`
- `500` `Failed to ingest the Word file.` (e.g. embedding provider down).
- `429` throttled: `{"detail": "Request was throttled. Expected available in N seconds."}`.
- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

**Frontend notes** — Send `FormData` without setting `Content-Type`. On an empty-document `400` or a `500`, the document row has already been created with status `failed` and still counts against quota. Refresh the list and offer delete, or rescue it by pasting text into `PUT /knowledge/sources/{id}/`. If the response is not `completed`, poll `GET /documents/{id}/`.

**Points** — this calls OpenAI (embedding the document's text; a 10-page document is ~1–2 points), charged to the tenant at its real cost. Returns `402` `{"detail": "You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan."}` when the tenant has less than 1 point, or `402` `{"detail": "Your subscription has expired. Please renew to continue."}` when its plan lapsed (staff are never blocked).

item.description: Documents are what you *uploaded*; knowledge content is what the bot actually answers from: the indexed pieces (~1200-char chunks) of every source (file upload, API sync, website crawl). Typical UI flow: `GET /knowledge/sources/` for the tabbed source list → open one source as a page (`GET /knowledge/sources/{document_id}/`) → edit and save the whole text (`PUT`), or fix single pieces via `/knowledge/{id}/`; `stats` feeds the overview. Everything is scoped to the caller: another tenant's piece is a plain 404, never a 403. Every write re-embeds synchronously, so a correction changes what the bot retrieves; if the embedding provider is down the write is rejected (400 for single pieces, 503 for a whole source) and the previous text stays live.

**What it does** — Lists every indexed piece the bot knows, across all your sources. Use it for an audit/search view; for reading a source as a page, use `GET /knowledge/sources/{document_id}/`.

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. Only pieces of your own documents. No rate limit.

**Request** — No body. Query params:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | string | No | Substring match on `content` |
| `document` | UUID | No | Only this document's pieces |
| `source_type` | enum | No | `file` \| `api` \| `website` |
| `document_name` | string | No | Case-insensitive contains on the document filename |
| `source_id` | string | No | Exact record/page id |
| `is_active` | bool | No | Owning document active / inactive |
| `edited` | bool | No | `true` = only hand-edited/added pieces, `false` = untouched |

| `page` | int | No | 20 per page |

**Response** — `200`, paginated `{count, next, previous, results}`. Each result:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Piece (chunk) id |
| `document`, `document_name` | UUID, string | Owning source |
| `source_type` | enum | `file` \| `api` \| `website` |
| `api_url` | string | Source URL for API/website, else "" |
| `is_active` | bool | Owning document's active flag |
| `position` | int | Order within the document |
| `content`, `char_count` | string, int | The text and its length |
| `metadata` | object | Free-form; `manually_added` / `manually_edited` flags appear here |
| `source_id` | string | Record/page id for API/website pieces, "" for files |
| `embedding_model`, `is_embedded` | string, bool | |
| `was_edited`, `edited_at` | bool, datetime \| null | Set when a human created/edited it |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | ISO datetime | |

**Errors**
- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

**Frontend notes** — Use `?edited=true` to review every correction currently in force. Show `char_count` and `source_type`. Pieces of an inactive document still appear here, but the bot does not answer from them.

request.description:
**What it does** — Adds one new piece of knowledge to one of your documents. It is embedded synchronously and searchable at once.

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. No rate limit and no document quota check (it costs one embedding call).

**Request** — JSON:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | UUID | Yes | Must be your own document; a foreign/unknown id is a validation error |
| `content` | string | Yes | Trimmed; must be non-empty |
| `metadata` | object | No | Stored as given, plus `manually_added: true` |

**Response** — `201` with the new piece (same fields as List). It is appended at the end of the document (`position` = last + 1), and `was_edited` is `true` (`edited_at` is set).

**Errors**
- `400` `{"detail": "A 'document' is required when adding knowledge."}`
- `400` `{"document": ["Invalid pk \"<id>\" - object does not exist."]}`: not your document.
- `400` `{"content": ["Content cannot be empty."]}` (or `This field is required.`).
- `400` `{"detail": "Could not embed the text: ..."}`: embedding provider down; nothing was saved.
- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

**Frontend notes** — Offer a document picker (from `GET /knowledge/sources/`). Insert the returned object straight into the list. Manually added pieces show `manually_added: true` in `metadata`, and in the source page's `sections`.

**Points** — this calls OpenAI (embedding the new text; a fraction of a point), charged to the tenant at its real cost. Returns `402` `{"detail": "You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan."}` when the tenant has less than 1 point, or `402` `{"detail": "Your subscription has expired. Please renew to continue."}` when its plan lapsed (staff are never blocked).

**What it does** — Corrects one piece's text (and/or metadata) and re-embeds it, so the bot is retrieved for the new wording immediately. `PUT /knowledge/{id}/` also exists; it is the same, except `content` becomes required.

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` (path) | UUID | Yes | |
| `content` | string | PATCH: no / PUT: yes | Trimmed, must be non-empty; defaults to the current text |
| `metadata` | object | No | MERGED into existing metadata (on PUT too), never replaced |
| `document` | UUID | No | Ignored; a piece never moves between documents |

**Points** — this calls OpenAI (embedding the new text; a fraction of a point), charged to the tenant at its real cost. Returns `402` `{"detail": "You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan."}` when the tenant has less than 1 point, or `402` `{"detail": "Your subscription has expired. request.description:
**What it does** — Fetches items from an external public JSON API and ingests them into the RAG system as one source (`source_type: "api"`). The whole SOURCE is imported: every page of a paginated response, plus each page's other top-level fields as an extra `response_metadata` record. **Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or the tenant API key (`X-API-Key: <key>` or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`). Any authenticated user, no role check. Feature `api_sync`: NOT available on the free tier (402). It requires the plan's `allow_api_sync`, unless an admin override is set; staff always have it. Rate limit: `ingest` scope, 10/min per account, shared with Crawl website / Sync API content. No document/storage quota check.

**Request** — JSON:

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `api_url` | string | Yes | Public http(s) URL; private/internal hosts are rejected |
| `document_name` | string | No | Default `API Content`; the same name re-syncs the same source |
| `items_key` | string | No | Default `results`; auto-detected (longest top-level list) when absent |
| `ai_analysis` | bool | No | Default `true`: the LLM describes each new/changed record, indexed next to the raw JSON |
| `full_refresh` | bool | No | Default `false` (incremental: only changed records re-embedded) |
| `max_pages` | int | No | Page cap; server default 200 |

**Response**
- `202` (background mode, typical in production): `{status: "queued", run_id, status_url, detail}`. Poll `status_url`.
- `200` (in-request mode): `{status: "success", run_id, pages_fetched, truncated, processed, chunks_created, items_new, items_updated, items_unchanged, items_removed, items_stored, items_analyzed, analysis_errors, analyses_rejected, items_protected, fields_total, fields_covered, field_coverage, records_with_issues, errors, schema_version, processing_version, validation, source_stats}`.

- `402` `Importing content from an external API isn't available on the free plan. Upgrade to enable it.`
- `400` `api_url is required`; an unsafe URL (`Only http and https URLs are allowed.`, `URL resolves to a private or reserved network address.`, …); `The API response contained no content to import.` (in-request mode).
- `422` the completeness check failed: `{detail, reason, validation, run_id}`. Existing knowledge is unchanged.
- `503` `Could not fetch content from the provided URL.` / `The import queue is unavailable. Please try again shortly.`
- `500` `Failed to process the fetched content.` / `An unexpected error occurred.`
- `429` throttled: `{"detail": "Request was throttled. Expected available in N seconds."}`.
- `401` missing/invalid JWT or API key (`Invalid API key.`, `API key is inactive.`).

**Frontend notes** — Branch on the status code, not on the body. Never block the UI: a full import makes one LLM call per record and can take minutes. `truncated: true` means `max_pages` stopped the import early. On `402` show the `detail` (feature not on the plan, or out of points — contact the administrator).

**Points** — this calls OpenAI (AI analysis of each record plus embeddings; if the points run out mid-way the run fails with the reason), charged to the tenant at its real cost. Returns `402` `{"detail": "You're out of points. Contact the administrator to renew your plan."}` when the tenant has less than 1 point, or `402` `{"detail": "Your subscription has expired. **Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or session cookie only. The tenant API key is **not** accepted here. **Admin (staff) only.**

**Request** — No body. `id` (UUID, path).

**Response** — `204 No Content`.

**Errors**
- `404` — unknown id.
- `401` — missing/invalid/expired credentials (`{"detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."}` or a token error).
- `403` — caller is signed in but not staff (`{"detail": "You do not have permission to perform this action."}`).

**Frontend notes** — Destructive: deleting the account also deletes all its WhatsApp contacts, and with them their sessions and message history. Confirm clearly; prefer `is_active: false` to pause.

response.name: 403 Forbidden — not an admin
404 Not Found — unknown or another tenant's id

**What it does** — Lists the customers who have messaged the tenant's WhatsApp number (contacts table / inbox sidebar).

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or session cookie only. The tenant API key is **not** accepted here. Any signed-in user; results are limited to contacts of the caller's own linked WhatsApp number (empty if none). Staff see all.

**Request** — No body. Query params (optional):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | string | No | Matches `phone_number`, `profile_name`. |
| `ordering` | string | No | `created_at`, `last_message_at`, `message_count`; default `-last_message_at`. |
| `is_active` | boolean | No | Filter. |
| `language_preference` | string | No | Filter (`ar`, `en`, …). |
| `page` | integer | No | Page size 20. |

**Response** — `200`, paginated `{count, next, previous, results}`; each result:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID string | Contact id. |
| `phone_number` | string | Customer's WhatsApp number. |
| `profile_name` | string \| null | WhatsApp profile name. |
| `language_preference` | enum | `ar` (default), `en`, `fr`, `es`, `de` — set by the `/lang` command. |
| `is_active` | boolean | |
| `message_count` | integer | Incoming messages received from this contact. |
| `last_message_at` | ISO datetime \| null | |
| `metadata` | object | Free-form, usually `{}`. |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | ISO datetime | |

**Errors**
- `401` — missing/invalid/expired credentials (`{"detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."}` or a token error).

**Frontend notes** — An empty list for a tenant usually means no WhatsApp account is linked yet — show a "Connect WhatsApp (contact admin)" empty state.

item.name: Messages (read-only)

request.description:
**What it does** — Lists logged WhatsApp messages — the conversation history between customers and the bot.

**Access** — JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <access>`) or session cookie only. The tenant API key is **not** accepted here. Any signed-in user; only messages of contacts on the caller's own linked number (empty if none). Staff see all.

**Request** — No body. Query params (optional):

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | string | No | Full-text match on `message_text`. |
| `ordering` | string | No | `created_at`; default `-created_at`. |
| `message_type` | string | No | `incoming` / `outgoing`. |
| `status` | string | No | Filter. |
| `user` | UUID | No | Filter by contact. |
| `session` | UUID | No | Filter by session. |
| `page` | integer | No | Page size 20. |

**Response** — `200`, paginated `{count, next, previous, results}`; each result:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID string | |
| `user` | UUID string | WhatsApp contact id. |
| `user_phone` | string | Contact's number. |
| `session` | UUID string \| null | |
| `message_type` | enum | `incoming` (from customer) \| `outgoing` (bot reply). |
| `message_text` | string | Message body. |
| `whatsapp_message_id` | string \| null | Meta id (outgoing rows after a successful send). |
| `status` | enum | `sent` (default), `delivered`, `read`, `failed` — currently always `sent` (status updates aren't stored). |
| `api_endpoint_used` | string \| null | Usually null. |
| `response_time_ms` | integer \| null | Reply generation time (outgoing). |
| `error_message` | string \| null | Set when reply generation failed. |
| `metadata` | object | Usually `{}`. |
| `created_at` | ISO datetime | |

**Errors**
- `401` — missing/invalid/expired credentials (`{"detail": "Authentication credentials were not provided."}` or a token error).

**Frontend notes** — For a chat-style view use `?user=<id>&ordering=created_at`. Each bot reply is currently logged **twice** (once when generated with `response_time_ms`, once after sending with `whatsapp_message_id`) — de-duplicate outgoing rows with identical text next to each other if needed.

**Access** — Public, no auth.

**Request** — No body.

**Frontend notes** — Use it for a status / maintenance banner; never put auth headers on it.
